Name: Alto de La Guarda (CA-ENP03)
Terrain: Forest ascent with some rocky sections, then open views towards the Valle del Río Lodar and Valle del Río Queriendo.
Why do it?: Substantial 8.5 km Saja-Besaya circuit with 650 m ascent: short in distance but a proper climbing day.
Notes: Naturea CA-ENP03. Official page provides route track and leaflet; ascent through oak woodland to Alto de La Guarda, then descent with views into the Lodar and Queriendo valleys.

Name: Braña de los Tejos (CA-ENP06)
Why do it?: One of Saja-Nansa's emblematic routes: mature oak and beech forest leading to a rare high-altitude grove of ancient yews at about 1,400 m.
Best Months / Conditions: Avoid poor weather; muddy after rain and snow is possible in winter. Official shorter option turns back before the Braña for about 8.7 km.

Name: Brañavieja — Cuchillón — Tres Mares
Why do it?: High Campoo ridge/summit day taking in Cuchillón and Tres Mares.
Best Months / Conditions: Snow-free, clear conditions; reassess for snow, ice, wind and visibility.
Parking: Brañavieja / Alto Campoo parking; confirm exact route start before walking

Name: Horcados Rojos
Why do it?: Classic high-mountain Picos objective with dramatic central-massif scenery.
Best Months / Conditions: Snow-free conditions with good visibility; snow, ice or poor visibility materially increase difficulty.
Trailhead / Start: El Cable, upper station of the Fuente Dé cable car
Notes: Official IGN/CNIG National Parks GPX: Horcados Rojos - Derivación, file 6-22-PRPNPE23-HORCADOS_ROJOS-DERIVACION.GPX.

Name: La Colina y Cascada del Avellano
Why do it?: Combines an Alto Asón summit/karst day with the Cascada del Avellano rather than treating the waterfall as an isolated stop.

Name: Laberintos del Asón
Terrain: Karst and limestone terrain with sections of scrambling/navigation complexity.
Why do it?: Distinctive Alto Asón limestone/karst day with much more character than a standard forest walk.
Exposure / Scrambling: Some scrambling; avoid in rain or fog.
Trailhead / Start: Collados del Asón area; exact labyrinth variant still needs verification

Name: Monte Camba — Tielve to Sotres (PR-PNPE 20)
Why do it?: Village-to-village Picos traverse between Tielve and Sotres through the eastern massif landscape.

Name: Monte Hijedo — ruta completa
Terrain: Forest tracks and paths; several stream crossings. GR 99 plus PR-BU-30 circular section.
Why do it?: Long immersion in one of Cantabria's major Atlantic oak forests, with mixed oak/beech woodland, streams and the Hijedo viewpoint.
Trailhead / Start: Riopanero / parking at start of forest track
Notes: Official description: 6.5 km from first parking to start of circular section, 8 km circular section, then return by the same approach; approximately 21 km total.

Name: Ordiales / Vegarredonda
Why do it?: Classic Lagos-side Picos day linking Vegarredonda with the Ordiales viewpoint.
Notes: PR-PNPE 5 Buferrera–Vegarredonda–Ordiales. Official Picos site states tracks are available for most signposted routes; direct official track link currently needs recovery.

Name: Peña Lusa y Porra del Trillo
Why do it?: Strong Alto Asón mountain objective combining Peña Lusa with Porra del Trillo.

Name: Peña Rocías y Hoyo Masallo
Why do it?: Limestone Alto Asón objective through the Peña Rocías / Hoyo Masallo landscape.

Name: Porracolina — Cordal de las Jorobas y vía normal
Why do it?: One of the defining Alto Asón summits, with a more adventurous Cordal de las Jorobas option and normal-route alternative.
Notes: Naturea CA-ENP09 Bustablado–Porracolina is an official 13 km route with downloadable track. This is an authoritative Porracolina approach; the record also covers the Cordal de las Jorobas / vía normal concept, so retain as a useful official variant rather than claiming identical geometry.

Name: Portillo de Lunada — Pico de la Miel — Castro Valnera
Terrain: High exposed mountain terrain; sections may be pathless.
Why do it?: Major local mountain day linking Lunada with Pico de la Miel and Castro Valnera.
Best Months / Conditions: Dry, clear conditions; avoid poor visibility.
Parking: Portillo de Lunada; confirm road and parking conditions before walking

Name: Ruta del Cares
Why do it?: The classic Cares gorge traverse: one of the defining walks of Picos de Europa.
Notes: Official IGN/CNIG National Parks GPX: Ruta del Cares, file 6-4-PRPNPE3-RUTA_DEL_CARES.GPX. Check current National Park alerts before walking because rockfall closures/restrictions can occur.

Name: Sendero de los Puentes (CA-ENP35)
Terrain: Monte Río de los Vados and Río Bayones woodland; multiple river/bridge crossings and notable trees.
Why do it?: Long forest circuit through Río Bayones / Monte Río de los Vados; a proper 15.8 km Saja-Besaya day rather than a short woodland stroll.
Best Months / Conditions: Check hunting calendar before going, particularly autumn/winter weekends.
Parking: Casa del Monte / Ucieda recreation area
Notes: Naturea CA-ENP35. Official page provides a route track and leaflet. Route lies in the Saja hunting reserve; check current hunting calendar for Vados Centro and Vados Sur.

Name: Sierra de Cocón — Oceño — Tresviso / San Esteban (PR-PNPE 34)
Why do it?: More adventurous eastern Picos traverse through the Sierra de Cocón and the Tresviso/San Esteban landscape.
Trailhead / Start: Oceño / San Esteban; choose direction before walking

Name: Sierra del Hornijo — Mazo Grande y Mortero de Astrana
Why do it?: Substantial Alto Asón ridge/massif day across Sierra del Hornijo, Mazo Grande and Mortero de Astrana.

Name: Urdón — Tresviso
Why do it?: One of the great steep approach walks of the eastern Picos, climbing from the Deva gorge to Tresviso.
Parking: Very limited space at Urdón; a secondary source recommends parking in La Hermida and approaching on foot if necessary.
Notes: Historic PR-PNPE 30 identity. Public route sources report that the former PR marking was later withdrawn, so do not rely on PR paint/signage alone.

Name: Vega de Ario
Why do it?: Classic western Picos refuge/meadow objective from the Lagos area with major massif views.
Trailhead / Start: Lagos de Covadonga / Lago Ercina area
Notes: PR-PNPE 4. Public track source identifies its geometry as the official IGN/CNIG National Parks route trace.

Name: Vega de Liordes
Why do it?: Dramatic high basin beneath the central Picos, reached by a sustained mountain approach.
Notes: Official IGN/CNIG National Parks route PR-PNPE25 Vega de Liordes; GPX and KML available.

Name: Acantilados de San Vicente (CA-ENP01)
Area: San Vicente de la Barquera / Western Coast
Why do it?: Official western-coast route adding a different cliff landscape from Costa Quebrada and Monte Buciero.

Name: Altos de Carmona (CA-ENP38)
Why do it?: Combines the historic village of Carmona with a proper climb onto the Sierra del Escudo de Cabuérniga.

Name: Bosque de Secuoyas de Monte Cabezón
Why do it?: Very short, accessible high-impact family woodland stop; keep separate from the 13.8 km Monte Corona hike.
Trailhead / Start: Monumento Natural de las Secuoyas del Monte Cabezón

Name: Canto Pilanco (CA-ENP10)
Why do it?: Compact forest hike through river woodland and mature beech forest, with an optional viewpoint over the south-western Saja-Besaya mountains.
Child Suitability: Strong short family/progression hike; optional viewpoint climb is short but steep.
Best Months / Conditions: Excellent autumn option. Check hunting calendar; avoid the steep viewpoint spur in adverse weather.
Trailhead / Start: Puente de Bárcena Sellano / Río Saja

Name: Cascada del Tobazo (CA-ENP route)
Why do it?: Short official Naturea waterfall route; useful family-scale hike and a distinct southern Cantabria landscape.

Name: Costa Quebrada — coastal walking route
Terrain: Coastal paths; route needs a canonical start/end variant selected before geometry is attached.
Why do it?: Signature local coastal landscape of cliffs, coves, beaches and geological formations close to home.
Notes: Government of Cantabria tourism material identifies the wider Costa Quebrada / Dunas de Liencres landscape and its walking paths. Keep as canonical local objective but select exact walking variant before marking a track verified.

Name: Demués — Lagos (PR-PNPE 08)
Why do it?: Alternative approach into the Covadonga lakes landscape from a quieter village trailhead; useful beyond the standard lakes circuit.

Name: Entorno de Tresviso (PR-PNPE 17)
Why do it?: A route focused on the immediate Tresviso landscape rather than repeating the much steeper Urdón approach.

Name: Hayedo de La Zamina (CA-ENP21)
Area: San Roque de Riomiera / Valles Pasiegos
Why do it?: Pasiego landscape, karst and a mature beech forest in one compact route.
Best Months / Conditions: Year-round, but avoid rainy/foggy days; particularly attractive in autumn.

Name: La Garma — Nacimiento del Pisueña (CA-ENP23)
Why do it?: Short official Pasiego route following the Pisueña towards its headwaters through traditional cabañas and limestone scenery.

Name: Lagos de Covadonga circuit
Why do it?: Classic accessible Picos circuit with exceptional scenery; particularly useful as a family mountain day.
Child Suitability: Strong family option: short, spectacular Picos scenery and low technical difficulty.

Name: Las Praizas de Cucayo (CA-ENP25)
Why do it?: Compact Liébana route through traditional invernales, hayedo and views towards Peña Dobres/Pica de Casanzo.

Name: Los Bosques del Monte Corona (CA-ENP33)
Why do it?: Turns the redwoods into a proper 13.8 km forest-and-viewpoint day through Monte Corona and the edge of Oyambre, rather than only a short stop at the sequoias.
Trailhead / Start: Parking de La Tejera / Monumento Natural de las Secuoyas

Name: Monte Buciero — Faros y Acantilados
Terrain: Coastal cliff and woodland paths; Faro del Caballo adds a long steep staircase.
Why do it?: Canonical Monte Buciero circuit combining Cantabrian cliffs, woodland, historic fortifications and the Faro del Caballo.
Best Months / Conditions: Dry conditions preferable; take particular care on steep/rocky terrain and the lighthouse stairs.

Name: Nacimiento del Asón / Cascada de Cailagua
Why do it?: Signature Alto Asón waterfall walk to the Nacimiento del Asón / Cascada de Cailagua.
Child Suitability: Possible family progression hike; longer than the short 4–6 km family options.
Trailhead / Start: Asón village / upper Río Asón valley
Notes: Public PR-S 14 track closely matches the canonical 9 km Cailagua route: 9.06 km and 269 m ascent.

Name: Peña Oviedo
Why do it?: Shorter Liébana/Picos foothill objective with strong views and less commitment than the high-mountain routes.
Trailhead / Start: El Cable / Fuente Dé for the official PR-PNPE22 descent towards Mogrovejo
Notes: Official IGN/CNIG National Parks GPX PR-PNPE22 Peña Oviedo (El Cable–Mogrovejo).

Name: Peñas de Bejes (CA-ENP07)
Why do it?: Shorter Liébana limestone route that gives us a useful middle ground below the major Picos objectives.

Name: Praderas de Ruyemas (CA-ENP29)
Why do it?: Short Pasiego circuit through traditional cabañales, beech woodland and views towards the Castro Valnera massif.
Child Suitability: Useful 5 km family progression hike with varied landscape.

Name: Pueblos de Sajambre (PR-PNPE 10)
Why do it?: Lower Picos cultural-and-landscape route linking the villages and forests of Sajambre.

Name: Puertos de Áliva
Why do it?: Cable-car-assisted route through major Picos scenery; a substantial distance with predominantly downhill walking.

Name: Ruta del Cubilón / Monte Aa
Terrain: Robledal de Monte Aa; route through mature oak woodland and the Árboles Milenarios area.
Why do it?: Short woodland circuit through Monte Aa, including the historic Cajigu del Cubilón / Árboles Milenarios area.
Child Suitability: Good family progression route through mature woodland.
Best Months / Conditions: Particularly attractive in autumn; otherwise usable much of the year.
Trailhead / Start: Ruente, access track toward Monte Aa
Parking: Parking/roadside space by the signed start after crossing the river in Ruente.
Notes: Public Cubilón track is a useful variant rather than an exact match to the 6.2 km board version: 8.46 km / 362 m, circular.

Name: Senda Fluvial del Nansa (CA-ENP34)
Area: Val de San Vicente / Herrerías / Saja-Nansa
Why do it?: Long but low-commitment riverside route that fills the gap between short family walks and mountain days.

Name: Sierra Breñas y Pico Candiano
Why do it?: Compact summit walk with enough ascent to feel like a proper hike without becoming a full mountain day.

Name: Vega de Llos (PR-PNPE 12)
Why do it?: Accessible Valdeón valley objective to the pastoral Vega de Llos, useful as a lower-commitment Picos day.

Name: Vega de Orandi
Why do it?: Short Picos route with real mountain landscape without requiring a long day.
Child Suitability: Short low-difficulty route suitable for building children's hiking distance.

Name: Canal de Camburero
Why do it?: Demanding classic Picos canal route; retained as a serious objective rather than an ordinary day hike.
Notes: Official CNIG National Parks catalogue includes RAM-PRPNPE19 Canal de Camburero.

Name: Collado Jermoso
Why do it?: One of the major Picos refuge objectives, with exceptional high-mountain scenery.
Best Months / Conditions: Snow-free mountain conditions; reassess for snow, ice and visibility.
Notes: Official CNIG catalogue includes Cordinanes–Collado Jermoso and Pandetrave–Collado Jermoso approaches; choose the intended approach before navigation.

Name: Jou de los Cabrones
Why do it?: Remote, serious central Picos refuge objective in spectacular limestone terrain.
Notes: Official CNIG National Parks catalogue includes RAM-PRPNPE18 Jou de los Cabrones.

Name: Pasá de Picayo
Why do it?: A genuinely committing and memorable Picos route rather than a routine walking objective.
Best Months / Conditions: Dry, stable conditions and good visibility.
Exposure / Scrambling: Exposed terrain; not a route to treat casually in poor conditions.

Name: Peña Lavalle — Pilar Este y vía normal
Why do it?: Technical-looking Alto Asón summit objective with Pilar Este and normal-route alternatives; requires route-specific verification before attempting.

Name: Porra del Mortillano — Faja del Campanu y vía normal
Why do it?: Serious Alto Asón mountain route with both Faja del Campanu and normal-route possibilities.

Name: Vega de Urriellu from Sotres / Pandébano
Why do it?: Iconic approach to the base of Picu Urriellu; one of the defining walking objectives in Picos de Europa.
Best Months / Conditions: Best treated as a snow-free mountain objective; conditions change substantially with snow or ice.
Trailhead / Start: Sotres / Collado Pandébano; choose exact parking/start variant before walking
Notes: CNIG provides official El Cable–Refugio de Vega de Urriellu GPX (principal + variant). This is useful official geometry but not the same approach as the canonical Sotres/Pandébano version in this record.
